questions.question: Which frontend language should the implementation use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Type-safe, modern implementation suitable for maintainable components and interactions.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Flexible implementation with no TypeScript compilation step.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is selected as a modern, maintainable default for the static marketing site.

questions.question: Which modern static frontend approach should be used?

options.label: React with Vite
options.description: Component-based React implementation with a fast development and build workflow.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: Full-featured React framework; more infrastructure than this static-only site needs.

options.label: Vanilla TypeScript
options.description: A lightweight static implementation without a component framework.

questions.rationale: React with Vite is a suitable modern static implementation because the request does not specify a framework and React provides reusable marketing-page sections.

questions.question: Which visual design direction should distinguish quthon from the reference site?

options.label: Bold dark enterprise
options.description: Charcoal and near-black surfaces, electric teal/cyan accents, crisp typography, and geometric cards.

options.label: Editorial light
options.description: Warm white canvas, cobalt accents, asymmetric editorial layouts, and large human-focused imagery.

options.label: Technical command center
options.description: Dense information design, grid systems, status indicators, and data-inspired visual motifs.

questions.rationale: A bold dark enterprise visual system provides strong differentiation while retaining the expected consulting-site trust and clarity.

questions.question: What structural patterns from the reference should be retained?

options.label: Enterprise pattern without copied branding
options.description: Use strong outcome-led messaging, solution cards, industry coverage, proof points, certifications, insights, and contact calls to action without SourceFuse branding or assets.

options.label: Minimal structure
options.description: Use only general enterprise consulting cues and avoid direct structural similarity.

questions.rationale: The plan should use structural inspiration only: clear value proposition, service pillars, proof, industries, insights, and conversion sections.

questions.question: What content and conversion features should be included in the first release?

options.label: Core enterprise marketing experience
options.description: Homepage, services overview, solutions, industries, proof/case studies, insights, company/about, and contact CTA.

options.label: Landing page only
options.description: A focused single-page marketing experience with fewer destination sections.

options.label: Full content site
options.description: Core experience plus detailed service and industry pages, insight articles, careers, and legal pages.

questions.rationale: The reference-inspired enterprise pattern warrants a complete but initially static marketing experience.

questions.question: Does the website need a database, file/object storage, queue, cache, or service-associated storage?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: No persistence, uploads, file serving, cache, queue, or service storage is needed for this static release.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for dynamic content, leads, or applications.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed relational database on Azure.

options.label: Cosmos DB
options.description: Globally distributed NoSQL database.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Azure storage for files, images, documents, media, or uploads.

options.label: Redis Cache
options.description: Distributed cache for dynamic application workloads.

questions.rationale: The requested website is static; no backend or persistent data store is currently specified.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to access application features or APIs?

options.label: No
options.description: The public marketing website does not require signed-in users.

options.label: Yes
options.description: The experience includes application features or protected APIs.

questions.rationale: A public consulting website and static conversion form do not require authenticated application features.
